rv.q: Actually, it’s more like three – making it a 360, all-round, head-spinning winner.
It is impossible not to be swept along by the giddily escalating mirth of Matt DiCarlo’s amiable production.
It made me laugh out loud more often than just about anything else I've seen in the last 12 months.
I’d say it takes near genius to fashion something this incorrigibly goofy.
For bungling wit matched with peerless physical comedy, you'd be hard pressed to find better in the West End.
I was crying helpless tears of laughter within the first five minutes, and at several other moments throughout.
But while the physical comedy is impeccably executed, the bare-bones story it’s running on will leave some craving a little more substance.
Farce this slick, this tongue-in-cheek, this quirkily British, will always draw laughter from a hugely appreciative audience.
This finely tuned machine of comic timing and theatrical chaos is possibly Mischief’s best work yet, offering audiences exactly what they have come to expect – and love – from this troupe.
If you like Mischief's previous work, you will love this.
Mischief is a creative, comedic powerhouse, and the clever storyline and talented cast make About Spies not only a spectacular spy spoof but also an outstanding show altogether.

About Spies is wonderful stuff, and highly amusing: this is a production company that has honed their craft, and their experience shines through in what is probably their most sophisticated show yet, at least in its technical aspects.
What could easily have come off the rails is majestically held together by Matt DiCarlo's razor-sharp direction.
What could easily have come off the rails is majestically held together by Matt DiCarlo’s razor-sharp direction.
Their latest show, an espionage spoof, improvised and scripted, strong on wordplay, is as silly and as funny and as absurd as their past productions.
This is an evening of daft, uncomplicated fun.
This is clearly going to be an enormous popular hit.
Mischief at their best, as finely worked as clockwork and exuberant as toddlers.

cn.t: Mischief Theatre delivers another crowd-pleasing hit with this 1960s spy spoof, earning praise for its sharp physical comedy, clever wordplay, and precisely choreographed farce that showcases the company's signature blend of slapstick and sophisticated humor.
